emergency.general: Dial 112 for the universal emergency number, or 100 (police), 108 (ambulance), or 101 (fire) directly. English is widely understood in major cities. In remote areas, ask hotel staff or bystanders to help communicate with emergency operators.

Rape is one of the fastest growing crimes in India.

healthcare.summary: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to India. Emergency numbers (112/102), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccination requirements, water safety, and travel insurance advice.
healthcare.costForTourists: Private healthcare in major cities is good quality and very affordable by Western standards — a GP visit may cost $5-15, hospital stays $50-200/day. However, quality drops dramatically in rural areas.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Comprehensive travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is essential. Serious conditions may require evacuation to a major city or even out of the country, which can cost tens of thousands of dollars.
healthcare.vaccinationsRecommended: Hepatitis A, typhoid, and tetanus are strongly recommended. Hepatitis B, Japanese encephalitis, rabies, cholera, and malaria prophylaxis may be advised depending on regions visited and duration.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Top private hospitals in Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Bangalore offer world-class care (Apollo, Fortis, Max). Public hospitals are heavily overcrowded with long waits. Rural healthcare infrastructure is very limited.

medications.prescriptionRules: A prescription is technically required for prescription medications, but enforcement is lax. Antibiotics and most common drugs are widely available OTC. Carry all medications in original packaging with a doctor's note. Use reputable pharmacies (Apollo, MedPlus) to avoid counterfeits.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is a controlled substance. Some products available with prescription. Many codeine-containing cough syrups are banned or restricted (like those used recreationally). Carry alternatives.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD stimulant medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Stimulants are controlled. Bring original prescription, doctor's letter, and only the amount needed. Declare at customs. A permit may be required from the Drugs Controller General of India.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications (diazepam, alprazolam, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Benzodiazepines require documentation. Carry a doctor's letter explaining medical necessity. Carry only what you need for your stay.

restrictedMeds.name: Sleep aids (zolpidem, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Some sleep aids are restricted. Carry alternatives if possible.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotics (morphine, tramadol, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Strong narcotics require strict documentation. Carry alternatives or minimal quantities with full documentation.

medications.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications with generic names in English. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, carry original prescriptions and a note explaining medical necessity. Some medications require an import permit from the Drugs Controller General of India — check before travel.
medications.generalAdvice: India's Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act imposes strict penalties for drug possession — even small amounts can lead to 6 months to 10 years imprisonment. Carry all prescription medications in original packaging with a doctor's letter and prescription. Pharmacies are widely available, but controlled substances require proper documentation.

scams.name: Gem Export Scam
scams.description: Shop owners offer gem export schemes for profit. You buy overpriced fake gems and the shop disappears.
scams.avoidance: Never agree to export schemes. Get independent verification from a certified gemologist.

scams.name: Train Ticket Scam
scams.description: Touts claim the ticket office is closed, then direct you to agencies selling overpriced tickets.
scams.avoidance: Go directly to the official counter or use IRCTC online.

scams.name: Fake Sadhu Blessing
scams.description: People dressed as holy men smear tikka on your forehead uninvited, then demand 500-2000 rupees.
scams.avoidance: Politely decline and walk away firmly.

scams.name: Prepaid Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: Drivers claim prepaid rates don't include tolls or surcharges, demanding extra payment.
scams.avoidance: Use the official prepaid counter inside the terminal. Use Uber/Ola as alternatives.

scams.name: SIM Card Identity Theft
scams.description: Street vendors use your passport copy for fraudulent SIM registrations.
scams.avoidance: Buy SIM cards only from official carrier stores.

connectivity.simOptions: Jio or Airtel tourist SIM at airport counters (passport + photo required, takes 1-24h to activate). Prepaid plans very cheap — unlimited data for $3-5/month.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi at most hotels and many cafes. Airport WiFi requires Indian phone number for OTP. Quality varies widely outside cities.
connectivity.bestOption: Airtel or Jio prepaid SIM for best coverage. Activation can take hours — buy at airport immediately on arrival. eSIM via Airalo as backup while local SIM activates.

cultural.tipping: 10-15% at restaurants if no service charge. Round up for taxis. Rs 20-50 for hotel porters. Tip tour guides Rs 200-500/day.
cultural.dressCode: Cover shoulders and knees at temples and religious sites. Remove shoes before entering temples, mosques, and homes. Women should carry a scarf for covering head at Sikh gurudwaras.
cultural.greetings: Namaste (palms together, slight bow) is the universal greeting. Handshakes common in business but avoid with opposite gender unless initiated. Use right hand for eating and passing items.
taboos: Pointing feet at people or religious objects
Using left hand for eating or passing items (considered unclean)
Wearing shoes inside temples or homes
Eating beef in Hindu areas or pork in Muslim areas
cultural.haggling: Expected and enjoyed at markets, auto-rickshaws, and street vendors. Not at fixed-price shops or malls. Start at 40-50% of asking price.

safety.lgbtSafetyNote: Same-sex relations were decriminalized by the Supreme Court in 2018, but social acceptance varies widely; discretion is advisable especially in rural areas and smaller cities.
safety.naturalDisasters: India is prone to monsoon flooding (June-September), cyclones along coastal areas, earthquakes in the Himalayan north, and extreme heat waves. Landslides occur in mountainous regions during monsoon season.
safety.pettyCrime: Petty theft, pickpocketing, and scams are widespread in tourist areas, train stations, and crowded markets. Common scams include gem schemes, fake tour guides, rigged taxi meters, and drugged food or drinks on trains.
safety.violentCrime: Violent crime against tourists is relatively uncommon but does occur. Sexual assault is a serious concern, particularly for women. Avoid isolated areas, especially at night.
safety.soloFemaleSafetyNote: Solo female travelers face heightened risk of harassment and assault; use trusted transport options, avoid traveling alone at night, stay in well-reviewed accommodations, and exercise constant situational awareness.
safety.notes: India offers incredible travel experiences but requires vigilance. Avoid the Kashmir region (except organized tours to specific areas), border areas with Pakistan, and northeastern states with active insurgencies. Political demonstrations and strikes (bandhs) can disrupt transport with little warning. Food and waterborne illness is very common — drink only bottled or purified water.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: e-Visa available (30-day, 1-year, or 5-year). Apply online before travel. Most Western nationals eligible for e-Visa.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: October-March (cool, dry season). Avoid April-June (extreme heat 40°C+) and July-September (monsoon). Hill stations are pleasant in summer.

stalenessWarnings.message: Some data in this profile may be outdated. Connect to the internet to refresh.

steps: File a police report immediately — get the report number, you will need it
Contact the US Embassy or nearest consulate: Contact the nearest US Embassy
Bring the police report + any ID you have (driver's license, copy of passport)
Apply for an Emergency Passport (usually issued within 1-2 business days)
Notify your travel insurance and airline of the situation
stolenPassport.notes: Keep a digital copy of your passport in cloud storage (Google Photos, iCloud) and email yourself a scan before travel.

steps: Go to the nearest police station (or call 100)
Bring ID or a copy of your passport if available
Request a written report — ask for an English copy or certified translation if needed
Keep the report number safe — required for insurance claims
For theft: list all stolen items with approximate values
policeReport.notes: In many countries, tourist police stations are available in major cities — they have English-speaking staff. Ask your hotel concierge for the nearest tourist police.

steps: If involved in an accident: do not move vehicles if anyone is injured
Call police (100) and ambulance (108) if there are injuries
Exchange contact, license, and insurance details with other parties
Document the scene with photos before moving vehicles
Contact your rental car company's emergency line
Contact your travel insurance's 24h assistance line
roadsideAssistance.notes: Traffic drives on the LEFT. An International Driving Permit (IDP) is required for most foreign licenses. Rental vehicles are available at major airports and cities.
